title: Personalization in the Patient Care Journey and Readmission Reduction
summary: Research on personalized patient engagement approaches during care transitions, with evidence on how tailored discharge planning and follow-up can reduce readmissions and unnecessary healthcare costs.

findings.personalization_value: Personalized care engagement leads to better member experience, higher quality of care, and reduction of avoidable healthcare costs. COVID-19 increased urgency as care delivery shifted and consumers became open to engaging in different ways.
findings.discharge_planning_focus: Research examined practical applications of personalization in discharge planning, specifically how post-admission engagement could reduce unnecessary readmissions. Transitions of care are a high-impact intervention point.
findings.consumer_research_findings: Consumer research reveals that patients respond to engagement that matches their communication preferences, health literacy level, and social determinant context. One-size-fits-all follow-up programs show significantly lower adherence.
findings.implications_for_patient_platforms: Patient engagement platforms must support: multi-channel outreach (text, call, app, portal), content personalization based on condition, health literacy, and language, care plan adherence tracking, and social determinant-aware resource recommendations.
findings.readmission_reduction_evidence: Supported discharge programs with personalized follow-up demonstrate measurable readmission reduction. Success correlates with: timeliness of first post-discharge contact, appropriateness of communication channel, and integration with primary care follow-up.

source: Consumer research examining personalization applications in discharge planning and care transitions for readmission reduction
